title: Police officer cleared in fatal shooting of Edmonton teen
article: An Edmonton police officer has been cleared of wrongdoing in the shooting death of a 17-year-old last February.
On the evening of February 4, 2011, 17-year-old Cyrus Green was shot and killed by police who were responding to reports of a mugging near the Coliseum LRT station.

According to information released at the time, the call resulted in a confrontation with Green in the parking lot of a nearby restaurant, during which Green allegedly lunged at an officer while armed with a knife and a baseball bat.
An investigation by the Alberta Serious Incident Response Team (ASIRT) determined that the officer who shot the teen was acting in self defense.

The ASIRT investigation revealed that Green ran towards police with an aluminum bat and a four-inch blade which was raised to shoulder height. When ordered to drop the weapons, Green told officers "you are going to have to shoot me."
Green was shot three times in the chest. His death was ruled as the city's fifth homicide of 2011.
An autopsy later found the presence of alcohol and marijuana in Green's system.

Edmonton police Chief Rod Knecht released a statement following the ruling, saying "although we are satisfied that this investigation has been resolved appropriately, it is nevertheless a tragedy that a young man has died."
